ringel-rangel.evidence: Complete two-page Dutch freely translated rules by Hendrik Cornilly, Spelgroep Hof van Watervliet, dated 29 March 2001 and hosted by Vlaams Spellenarchief/Spellenlab. Explicit unofficial translation of Geni Wyss HABA 1993 Ringel-Rangel, matching BGG 10509 wooden turtle/ring dexterity game. Both pages fully read: 24 turtles/20 balls, player color and two shared turtle piles, optional zero-to-three branches, matching entry/goal, one-finger push and legal board support, fallen-piece penalty collection, neutral own-color balls, error-free return of a ball, end after both piles exhausted and fewest penalties wins. Native text intact. Matching original French last page independently confirms penalty-based ending, but its archived PDF includes an unrelated opening page, so that earlier incomplete original remains unaccepted as main rules. Translation authority is unofficial; the Dutch account describes an extra penalty turtle from an opponents personal supply while French says from the board, so that specific transfer procedure is not certified. Useful full translated source with explicit limitation, not a publisher original or full accuracy audit. Summary opposite victory condition recorded separately.

afrikan-t-hti-retkikunnat.evidence: Complete original Finnish Peliko/Martinex 2014 Afrikan tahti: Retkikunnat expansion rulebook, linked by current publisher product page, matching named BGG 165320, Joonas Tupala/Aleksi Michelsson. All 12 PDF pages (cover, printed 1–10, final continuation/credits) read. Includes layered 30+30 treasure tokens, character setup and 300 pounds, three symbols of each type to form expedition, three ordered turn phases, seven expedition/four hand-card limits, movement/events, equipment selling, five danger dice and robbery with rerolls/penalties, diamond or post-diamond horseshoe return to Cairo/Tangier, card/Slave Coast/rain clarifications, five/six-player two-symbol variant and fast game. Setup/token table and combat page visually checked; labelled token-column note restores icon-only headings. Complete main expansion book, not four-page quick-start sheet. Requires original Afrikan tahti board/die/money and inherits its basic rules; ordinary transport/turning costs and winning are restated, but base-only rules and exhaustive individual card text are not claimed. Native extraction has illustrative card overlap and missing symbol graphics; unchanged original PDF remains authoritative. Finnish accepted under user original-language preference; no summary accuracy audit.

roope-set-liikemiespeli.evidence: Complete original Finnish Tactic Roope-Seta Liikemiespeli manual, four PDF pages, publisher product code 02669. Entire original text read: 20000 initial cash, clockwise die movement, 10000 shares, all seven share benefits and three-share unlimited-use majority, own-property gold rolls, rent/share differences, start income/collection spaces, freely negotiated player share/gold trades, 7000 bank resale, gold bought for 10000 but scored 5000, lack-of-cash handling/bank payment restriction, ordered turn, exhaustion of central gold and wealth scoring. Original page-three Free Trade panel visually checked; native text contains minor duplicate decorative overprint but main rules readable. Earlier Doczz transcription matches, original publisher PDF preferred and retained unchanged. Finnish original accepted under user language preference. Specific false no-player-trading summary statement recorded separately; no full summary audit.

pegity.evidence: Complete original English Parker Brothers Pegity instruction folder in two imposed PDF scan pages, openly hosted by Association for Games and Puzzles International Game Catalog. Correct BGG 6247 five-in-a-row pegboard game, not the unrelated 1894 geography Pegity. Both whole page images fully read and main directions/partners/bonus game manually transcribed to avoid mosaic-art OCR garbage. Includes two-to-four-player color setup, empty-hole single-peg turns, blocking, uninterrupted horizontal/vertical/diagonal five-in-row victory, shared-color four-player Partners with expressly permitted signals, and separately labelled 4-5-6 misere peg-removal game. Original diagrams retained unchanged; historical sales text and non-game mosaic suggestions omitted only from canonical selection. Source archive canonical hostname with ordinary browser content negotiation supplied the complete PDF; first www request 406, official Hasbro PDF direct 403, and mirrored response with PHP-warning prefix are recorded failed leads, not accepted originals. Minor summary Partners no-communication statement conflicts with original permitted signals, but no full summary audit or Verified verdict is implied.
